selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What is the second truth called in this passage?
questions.answer: It is called absolute dominicality.

questions.question: What signs in the universe point to this truth?
questions.answer: The passage points to the wise and caring management seen all through the universe, especially in living things and how they are raised and developed.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the way this care happens everywhere?
questions.answer: It says it happens in the same general way everywhere, yet in surprising forms.

questions.question: Why can this absolute dominicality not have any partner?
questions.answer: Because its important goals would be harmed if even the smallest thing were linked to a partner beside Allah.

questions.question: What are some of those goals of dominicality named in the passage?
questions.answer: They include showing beauty, announcing perfection, displaying precious works, and making hidden excellences known.

questions.question: Why does the passage pay special attention to small living things and particular cases?
questions.answer: Because those great purposes are gathered and shown clearly even in tiny and specific creatures.

questions.question: What would happen if people turned toward causes instead of the One who planned everything?
questions.answer: They would be turned away from the true source and purposes, and that would go against dominicality.

questions.question: According to the passage, how does such a wrong turning relate to the nature of dominicality?
questions.answer: It is described as opposing and fighting against its very nature.

questions.question: What does the passage say the Qur’an does because of this truth?
questions.answer: It says the Qur’an again and again points people to Allah’s oneness and declares His freedom from any partner.

questions.question: How strongly does the passage describe the Qur’an’s guidance to unity?
questions.answer: It describes that guidance as constant and very widespread, reaching even to its verses, words, letters, and their forms.

questions.question: Which part of the universe is especially mentioned as showing caring rule?
questions.answer: Living things are especially mentioned.

questions.question: What two qualities describe the hidden hand working through the universe?
questions.answer: It is described as wise and compassionate.

questions.question: What two activities in living things are named as examples of this rule?
questions.answer: Their nurturing and their development are named.

questions.question: What conclusion does the passage draw from these signs?
questions.answer: It concludes that they are a clear proof of absolute dominicality.

questions.question: What word in the passage shows there is no doubt about this proof?
questions.answer: It says this is so without doubt.

questions.question: Why would adding a partner to Allah be a serious problem even in one tiny creature?
questions.answer: Because even there it would spoil the goals that dominicality wants to bring about.

questions.question: What are people called in the passage when it speaks about their attention and understanding?
questions.answer: They are called conscious beings.

questions.question: Why is turning conscious beings toward causes wrong according to the passage?
questions.answer: Because it pulls them away from the true planner and from the real purpose behind creation.

questions.question: What attitude of the Qur’an toward Allah is mentioned near the end?
questions.answer: The Qur’an often declares Allah’s perfect purity and greatness above any partner.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the Qur’an’s verses and even smaller parts of it?
questions.answer: It says not only the verses and words but even the letters and their shapes guide people to Allah’s unity.

questions.question: What truth is being explained in this passage?
questions.answer: The passage explains absolute dominicality.

questions.question: What everyday observation helps prove this truth?
questions.answer: We can see that living things are cared for, grown, and managed in wise and merciful ways.

questions.question: Does the passage present this care as random or purposeful?
questions.answer: It presents it as purposeful.

questions.question: Which words in the passage support the idea of purpose?
questions.answer: The passage supports it by describing the working as wise, compassionate, and aimed at important goals.
